newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's trade surplus rises sharply in July.
newsitem.headline: Germany's trade surplus rises sharply in July.

text.p: Germany's trade surplus rose to 10.9 billion marks ($7.17 billion) in July from 7.0 billion in June and from 6.0 billion marks in July 1995, the Federal Statistics Office said.

The current account, the broadest measure of trade in goods and services, remained in deficit by 4.4 billion marks, widening from a 2.1 billion mark deficit in June, but narrower than a 5.4 billion mark shortfall in the year-earlier month.

Exports rose to 67.5 billion marks in July from 60.9 billion in the previous month and 58 billion in the year earlier month, while imports increased to 56.6 billion marks from 53.9 billion marks and 52 billion marks, respectively.

For the first seven months of 1996, Germany showed a trade surplus of 56.5 billion marks, up from 50.5 billion marks in the same period of 1995, and a current-account deficit of 13.1 billion marks, up from 9.5 billion.
